notes: HTTP-first tier sufficed (robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow, homepage 200, sitemap fully reachable). Site is Shopify (bouclair-production.myshopify.com) with a Vue-hydrated storefront theme. Discovery: pulled sitemap.xml -> sitemap_collections_1.xml (375 collections, EN) and the /fr/ equivalent (375 collections, FR-CA), then scanned every collection URL/title/meta for holiday vocabulary (Christmas, Halloween, Diwali, Easter, Valentine, Thanksgiving, New Year, Indian festivals, Mother's/Father's Day, St. Patrick's, etc.), cross-checked the rendered homepage main-nav collection links (~80 links, none Christmas/holiday - off-season, Sept nav has no seasonal branch live), and spot-checked search?q=halloween/diwali (client-rendered, inconclusive but no corroborating sitemap evidence either) plus /pages/ sitemap for editorial holiday pages. FOUND: exactly 5 Christmas collections (christmas-decorations, christmas-decorative-objects, christmas-ornaments-and-tree-skirts, christmas-throw-pillows, nutcrackers) - each has its own canonical PLP URL, English title, and (confirmed via meta description) a Christmas-specific 2025 return-policy notice baked into the page metadata, proving these are genuine, actively-maintained Christmas categories, not stubs. Each has a verified French-Canadian mirror (fr/collections/decorations-de-noel, decorations-de-noel-1, ornements-de-noel-jupes-de-sapin, coussins-de-noel) whose hreflang/canonical tags resolve back to the same 5 English collections 1:1 - no additional French-only holiday categories exist, so French duplicates were not double-counted. No shared parent 'Christmas' grouping collection/nav node exists (checked /collections/christmas, /holiday, /holiday-shop, /festive - all 404), so the 5 are listed as flat leaves per the site's actual (parentless) structure, not under an invented grouping row. QTY: the live product-count widgets are Vue client-side placeholders (raw HTML only contains Vue template markup, no real number), so qty was established via the store's own products.json collection endpoint (same endpoint verified accurate against non-seasonal collections like /collections/lighting and /collections/all, which return real product arrays). All 5 Christmas collections returned {"products":[]} (0) as of 2026-09-04. Given today is early September and the Christmas-specific return-policy metadata references the 2025 season, this reads as a genuine, permanent Christmas taxonomy that is currently unstocked pre-season rather than an abandoned/fake category - recorded as qty 0 with a MANUAL REVIEW flag rather than qty null, since the count (0) was actually established, not unknown. EXCLUDED as non-seasonal or failing the PLP/marketing test: 'Autumnal Nest' and 'Festive Lodge' (collections/autumnal-nest, collections/festive-lodge) - these are two of dozens of similarly-named interior-design mood/style collections on this site (Bogota, Sahara, Nordic Bliss, Trendy Nook, Mint Room, Magic Charm, etc.); no holiday-specific meta/return-policy signal, not on the same structural footing as the Christmas branch, so per rules SS6/SS9 they are loose seasonal-style names, not a genuine occasion taxonomy. 'Seasonal Greenery' and 'Seasonal Scents' - generic year-round merchandising labels ('seasonal' as a department, not a specific holiday), no holiday association in title/meta. 'Under $25/$50/$100 Gift Guide - Mother's Day' (collections/under-25-gift-guide-mother-day, under-50-gift-guide-mother-day, under-100-gift-guide-mother-day) - inspected actual product.json contents: each is a cross-category, price-tiered curated gift list (hand soap, artificial greenery, decorative bowls, placemats, candles, terrariums all mixed together) with no coherent product type, matching the rules' explicit 'cross-category audience gift-guide with no coherent product type' exclusion and the shared core's explicit 'Gift Guide' exclusion example; page title itself is just 'Under $25', confirming it's a price-tier landing page, not a Mother's Day product category. No broader/non-gift-guide Mother's Day category exists on the site, and no Father's Day category was found anywhere in the collections or pages sitemaps. /pages/holiday-centerpieces and /pages/holiday-mantel-guide are editorial content pages (0 product-tile elements, no product grid) - excluded as blog/inspiration pages, not PLPs. No Halloween, Diwali, Easter, Valentine's Day, Thanksgiving, New Year, or any Indian-festival (Holi, Rakhi, Eid, Navratri, etc.) categories were found in either the English or French sitemap collection lists, the homepage nav, or the pages sitemap - concluded genuinely absent for this company (Bouclair's seasonal assortment is Christmas-only), not merely unsearched.
